subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the rank of the matrix with rows (1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 4) and (0, 1, 2).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the rank of this matrix.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Test the 3×3 determinant
steps.margin_note: First mark. Start with the largest minor — the whole determinant. It comes to 0, so the rank is less than 3 and you must look at a smaller minor.
steps.memory_tip: Start with the largest minor — the whole determinant. It is 0, so the rank is less than 3.
lines: So the rank is less than 3.

recall.must_convey: That the 3×3 determinant is computed first, comes to 0, and that this rules out rank 3.
accept: take the full determinant first, it is zero so the rank cannot be three
the three by three determinant is zero so the rank is less than three
expand the determinant and get zero
three by three determinant zero kabatti rank three kaadu
the largest minor is zero so we go down a size

steps.why: Rank is the size of the largest non-zero minor, so the search always starts at the top and works down. A zero determinant only rules out the largest size.
common_mistakes: Answering 0 as soon as the determinant is zero.

steps.label: Find a non-zero 2×2 minor
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Only ONE non-zero 2×2 minor is needed — you are not checking them all. The top-left block gives 3 − 4 = −1, which is enough.
steps.memory_tip: Only ONE non-zero 2×2 minor is needed; you are not checking them all.
lines: Take the 2×2 minor from the top-left:
A non-zero 2×2 minor exists, so the rank is 2.

recall.must_convey: That one non-zero 2×2 minor is found (value −1), which is enough to fix the rank at 2.
accept: find any two by two minor that is not zero, the top left gives minus one, so the rank is two
one non zero two by two minor is enough so rank equals two
the minor one two two three is minus one which is not zero so rank is two
oka two by two minor zero kaakapothe rank two

steps.why: Finding ONE non-zero minor of a given size is enough — the definition asks whether one exists, not whether all of them do.
common_mistakes: Checking every 2×2 minor and wasting time.
Finding a 2×2 minor that happens to be zero and concluding the rank is 1.

insider_note: Show the 3×3 determinant is 0 FIRST, then produce one non-zero 2×2 minor. Both halves are needed: the zero rules out 3, the non-zero establishes 2.
